newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says strong dollar in U.S. interests.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says strong dollar in U.S. interests.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Monday reiterated that a strong dollar is in the U.S. interest and that the administration policy toward the currency had not changed.
"I think a strong dollar is in the interest of the United States," Rubin told reporters after moderating a panel discussion on microcredit.

Asked about the prospects for a discussion of exchange rates at the upcoming meeting of Group of Seven officials in Berlin this weekend, Rubin replied that the subject would be one of many to come up.
"I can not imagine any more than two finance ministers getting together anywhere in the world and not discussing, amongst other things, currencies," Rubin said.

Rubin said he had not seen the agenda for the meeting. But he said currencies along with other key issues, such as the macroeconomic performance of the various nations and trade, would be discussed either formally or informally.
"These are the kinds of things you talk about when you go to finance ministers' meetings," he added. He declined to comment on his expectations of the outcome of such discussions.

Asked what the G7 might discuss in terms of spurring Japan's economy, the U.S. Treasury Secretary replied, "In terms of Japan, I'll just repeat what I always say: They and we have an interest in having a strong economy and one that is led by domestic demands, and I'm sure we will be discussing the issues that are relevant there too."
Turning to the subject of inflation in the United States, Rubin was asked if he was concerned that it might begin to rise.
"You always have to be watchful about inflation," he said. "On the other hand, as you look out, it looks to me that the prospects are very encouraging for as far out as I care to look."

In his opening remarks at the panel discussion on microcredit, Rubin said the Clinton administration was very committed to the idea of encouraging microenterprise activity. He also said that it is one issue he would like to raise informally at the G7 meeting this weekend. He said he thought it would be important for the group to raise its profile in that area.
